structural_principle: Linear antisymmetric content cannot appear in fully-symmetric M_native at n >= 3; only quadratic (sum-of-squared-differences) survives.

predictions.name: P1_newton_identity_holds_for_all_3body_rows
predictions.details: Newton identity 3*(a^2+b^2+c^2) = s1^2 + Delta^2 verified on 76/76 rows

predictions.name: P4_two_body_is_structurally_distinct
predictions.details: For (1,2): R*[s1^2+Delta^2] = 12*(9+1) = 120, but observed M_2(1,2) = 27.  The rewriting does not apply at n=2; CR130 explicitly notes this.

wrong_controls.name: WC2_no_4body_rows_in_sample
wrong_controls.details: CR119 currently has no 4-body partitions; CR130_PRED_1 is forward-blind only -- no in-sample data to overfit the conjecture

wrong_controls.name: WC3_structural_argument_separated_from_data
wrong_controls.details: The symmetry argument (why linear antisymmetric vanishes at n >= 3) is representation-theoretic and independent of CR119 data.  In-sample verification confirms the algebraic IDENTITY, not the structural argument.

wrong_controls.name: WC4_prefactor_n_dependence_explicitly_unresolved
wrong_controls.details: Whether the prefactor in M_n = (prefactor) * Sum a_i^2 scales as R*n (giving R*D=36 for n=3 and 4*R=48 for n=4), or follows another pattern, is acknowledged as an open question.  CR130 does not claim resolution.

wrong_controls.name: WC5_two_body_special_case_explicitly_noted
wrong_controls.details: CR130 does NOT claim the n >= 3 form extends to n=2.  The 2-body formula remains as CR128 locked it.  The structural break at the 2->3 boundary is documented.

wrong_controls.name: WC6_4body_conjecture_clearly_provisional
wrong_controls.details: CR130_PRED_1 is explicitly marked FORWARD_BLIND_NO_IN_SAMPLE_DATA.  The conjecture rests on extrapolation, not derivation.  Future 4-body data either confirms (locks v1.0) or falsifies (triggers v1.1).
